guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our slight lean toward North Texas comes primarily from the passing matchup. Our numbers rate North Texas among the most efficient passing offenses in the country, while Navy has struggled badly in that area defensively. Tayven Jackson completed 95 of 128 passes for 1,187 yards through four games, and Justin Stevenson and Corri Milliner had each surpassed 275 receiving yards. We see multiple ways for North Texas to challenge the part of Navy’s defense our numbers trust least.

The counterweight is Navy’s rushing attack against a North Texas defense that has shown vulnerability on the ground. Navy averaged 376 rushing yards and 6.90 yards per carry through its first two games, while North Texas allowed 337 rushing yards to Texas State. We are not treating either small sample as proof, but that matchup gives Navy a credible path to controlling possessions and keeping the game tight. That is why our disagreement with the market is modest and why the available price does not provide enough value for us.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the defining matchup is Jackson and the North Texas passing game against Navy’s pass defense. Navy had not produced a takeaway through its first two games, while Jackson had thrown only two interceptions through four. We would not project future turnover results from those samples alone, but North Texas protecting the ball while generating efficient pass plays would make it harder for Navy to shape the game around its rushing offense and possession time.

recent_game.fact: Navy lost 38-30 at Florida Atlantic on Sept. 12, falling to 1-1 overall and 0-1 in the American Conference.
Navy trailed Florida Atlantic 38-7 before scoring 23 consecutive points over the final 16 minutes.

Jackson Gutierrez replaced injured quarterback Braxton Woodson against Florida Atlantic and rushed seven times for 75 yards and one touchdown while completing 6 of 12 passes for 100 yards and two touchdowns.
Navy did not force a turnover against Florida Atlantic and had not recorded a takeaway through its first two games.

quarterback.fact: Braxton Woodson rushed for 96 yards and one touchdown on 12 carries against Florida Atlantic before leaving on the first drive of the third quarter with a lower-body injury.
Through two games, Woodson averaged 148 rushing yards per game and 8.46 yards per carry, with four rushing touchdowns.
Woodson rushed for a career-high 200 yards and three touchdowns on 23 carries in the season-opening 42-15 win over Towson.
Jackson Gutierrez was being used at both quarterback and running back in 2026.
Gutierrez played both quarterback and running back against Towson, rushing eight times for 31 yards and the first two touchdowns of his career.

offensive_personnel.fact: Center Cam Nichols started the first two games at guard because Navy believed that alignment put its best five offensive linemen on the field.
Sophomore Malcolm Johnson started each of Navy's first two 2026 games at offensive tackle after starting seven games there as a freshman in 2025.
Running back Vic Listorti, who played only five games in 2025 while dealing with a hamstring injury, opened 2026 with a career-high 81 rushing yards and his first career touchdown against Towson.
Listorti rushed four times for 35 yards and lost a fumble against Florida Atlantic.
Wide receiver Luke Hutchison had one reception for 27 yards against Florida Atlantic after receiving no touches against Towson.
Navy had six players on its depth chart who arrived as quarterbacks and had moved to other positions or were splitting time between quarterback and another position.

Tre Jones III, Isaiah Bryant and Christian Cromer made their first career starts on offense against Towson; Charles Robinson, Michael Barrow and Vic Listorti made their first career starts against Florida Atlantic.
